application_guidance.input_pattern: An unconstrained NC–SC minimax problem with only fresh bounded-variance joint gradients and explicit primal-gap/dual-residual budgets.
read_original_when: Changing oracle information, finite-dimensional uniformity, initialization, output metric or stopping convention.
Using any imported construction or inner-solver lemma beyond this source-linked statement/proof map.
sensitive_conditions: Do not replace the initial gradient residual G by a distance without rescaling through μ||y0−y*(x0)||≤||∇_y f(x0,y0)||≤L||y0−y*(x0)||.
Do not apply the lower bound to a value oracle, reuse oracle, HVP or free exact-prox interface.
Do not replace the all-path fixed call cap by a worst-instance expected cost.
The local statistical C term and explicit additive localization logarithm are essential for uniform parameter dependence.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Per-instance probability at least 2/3 under a fixed integer all-path cap on original calls. Intermediate expected work alone is not this guarantee.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Universal c,C0,C1,κ0; upper envelope Λ^{10} explicitly defined and independent of G.
complexity_scope.oracle: One fresh same-point joint gradient pair per raw call; fixed kernel, conditional unbiasedness and joint conditional variance at most σ² everywhere. No values/reuse/HVP/free prox.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Primal xhat, not necessarily a queried point; Euclidean true primal gradient norm ||∇Φ(xhat)||≤ε.
complexity_scope.resource: Original fresh joint-gradient calls, including every random multilevel call; uniform over all finite dimensions.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper: an implementable fresh-gradient algorithm. Lower: all measurable adaptive randomized algorithms with arbitrary unbounded queries and arbitrary final primal output; finite hard dimensions can grow with the horizon.

content.intended_use: Use the paper's minimax characterization with its actual oracle, unrestricted algorithm class, initialization promise and fixed-budget success convention.

proofs.locator: §4 pp.8–11; Theorem F.5 p.37; Theorem G.1 pp.38–39; §H p.39
map: Import Theorem F.5: for jointly ℓ-smooth, α-strongly convex/μ-strongly concave g with α≥ℓ/4 and expected initial weighted error at most E0, expected saddle gap η costs at most KΛ_g^8[√κ_g log(2+κ_g E0/η)+σ²/(μη)], where κ_g=ℓ/μ and Λ_g=1+log(2+κ_g)+log(2+σ²/(μη)). This includes random g and random initialization satisfying uniform assumptions and the expected energy bound. Lemmas F.1–F.4 are imported, not independently reproved here.

Theorem G.1 applies that interface to g_c=f+L||u−c||², with ℓ=3L, α=L. With η_c=ε²/(10^6L) and T=ceil(10^6LΔ/ε²), unconditional descent yields average E||m(x_t)||²≤16ε²/10^6 and total movement bounded by Δ+Tη_c.
The first subproblem has known energy O(G²/μ+κΔ). Strong monotonicity and the movement bound control later expected warm starts without further G dependence.

Choose R uniformly and independently of coarse solves. Refine the same g_{x_R} from its stored output once to η_f=ε²/(10^6κL). Equation (9) transfers this saddle-gap accuracy to E||∇Φ(xhat)||²≤176ε²/10^6<ε²/12.
Coarse calls contribute tilde O(A+B), fine calls contribute tilde O(√κ+C); fine deterministic work is absorbed by A in the nontrivial regime. Add the one explicit cold-start logarithm.

For a known expected TOTAL original-call bound W, stop at ceil(12W) raw calls and output zero if exceeded. Coupling with the untruncated run gives truncation probability ≤1/12; the squared-gradient estimate gives output failure ≤1/12. Success is at least 5/6, sufficient for Definition 3.3.
proofs.omitted_details: Full proofs of the imported inner-solver lemmas F.1–F.4 are not reproduced or independently certified. This is a literature proof map, not a new local transfer theorem.
proofs.reading_coverage: Read original-PDF statements and proof of F.5/G.1/H and visual §4 architecture; not all Appendix F proofs.

map: E.3 gives Ω(A) using an exact joint-gradient oracle with zero initial dual residual; its hiding argument exposes one chain vertex per call, protects large queries, and includes the final output as a dummy query.

C.5 gives Ω(LΔ/ε²+B) with G0=0 through fixed Bernoulli-gated oracle revelations. Its auxiliary process is defined on every trajectory; independent primal/dual frames and flat gates couple true and auxiliary transcripts until a projection violation.

D.1 gives Ω(C) for σ>0 using two globally admissible signs with disjoint successful primal sets. A uniform per-query conditional KL bound sums across adaptive calls; data processing and Pinsker force the testing cost. Its initial residual is zero and its gap fits the universal nontrivial regime after increasing constants.
Corollary B.3 gives Ω(D_G) for κ≥8192 and Δ≥80ε²/L using exact gradients and a dual chain; the b≤1 case is vacuous. Its N=0 case uses the zero-query testing obstruction.

§H combines the maximum of these four separate admissible lower bounds, which is at least one quarter of their sum, and absorbs universal regime constants. Its logarithmic comparison preserves explicit G dependence.
proofs.omitted_details: Only the listed lower statements and selected proof portions were read. Full constructions, model-membership calculations, dimensional calibration and all auxiliary lemmas in Appendices A–E remain imported source interfaces; no Hard Family record or independent reconstruction is asserted.
proofs.reading_coverage: Original-PDF statement/proof portions for B.3,C.5,D.1,E.3, initial-image §5.1 and original-PDF §H.

assumptions: L≥μ>0, Δ,σ,G≥0 and ε>0; f:R^{d_x}×R^{d_y}→R is differentiable and jointly globally L-smooth in Euclidean norm.
For every x, f(x,·) is globally μ-strongly concave on unconstrained R^{d_y}. Φ(0)−inf_x Φ(x)≤Δ and ||∇_y f(0,0)||≤G. G bounds a gradient residual, not a dual distance.

The oracle is a Markov kernel fixed before interaction. At any query z_t=(x_t,y_t), one raw call returns a fresh same-point joint vector G_t with E[G_t|F_{t−1},z_t]=∇f(z_t) and E[||G_t−∇f(z_t)||²|F_{t−1},z_t]≤σ², globally at every query.
Only this gradient information is supplied: no values, finite-sum index, same-sample multi-point evaluation, sample-reuse interface, HVP or free proximal oracle.

An algorithm has an independent internal random seed; queries and final primal output are arbitrary measurable functions of the appropriate transcript and seed. Dense, nonlinear and unbounded-norm queries are allowed. No zero-respecting, linear-span, Krylov, obliviousness or determinism restriction is imposed.
statement.conclusion: c(A+B+C+D_G) ≤ T_all^loc(L,μ,Δ,σ,G,ε) ≤ C1 Λ^{10}[A+B+C+√κ log(2+κ²G²/ε²+κ²LΔ/ε²)]. Consequently T_all^loc=tilde Θ(A+B+C+D_G). Λ and its power ten are independent of G: suppressed factors are logarithmic in κ,LΔ/ε²,κ²σ²/ε² only. Constants are universal. In particular, C is paid once by final refinement; it is neither omitted nor multiplied by all outer stages.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean spaces R^{d_x}×R^{d_y}, arbitrary finite dimensions. Initial point (0,0). Φ(x)=max_y f(x,y), κ=L/μ, log_+(u)=log(max{1,u}) for u≥0. Define A=√κ LΔ/ε², B=κLΔσ²/ε⁴, C=κ²σ²/ε², D_G=√κ log_+(G/(ε√κ)). Define Λ=1+log(2+κ)+log(2+LΔ/ε²)+log(2+κ²σ²/ε²). T_all^loc is the least fixed integer N for which an admissible algorithm makes at most N original oracle calls and returns xhat satisfying P(||∇Φ(xhat)||≤ε)≥2/3 on every pair (f,O) in the class and every finite dimension; absent such N, it is +∞.
statement.parameter_domains: κ≥κ0 and LΔ≥C0ε², with the preceding nonnegative finite budgets and ε>0. The class is the union over all finite primal and dual dimensions, rather than a fixed-small-dimension claim. σ=0 and G=0 are included.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist universal constants c,C0,C1,κ0>0 such that the bounds hold for every admissible parameter tuple in the stated regime. The upper witness succeeds on every admissible instance and every finite dimension under a deterministic raw-call cap, with probability over its seed and oracle replies. Lower bounds cover every admissible randomized algorithm; a finite hard-instance dimension may depend on its proposed horizon and parameters. Separate fixed hard distributions supply the four lower-bound terms; they are not one direct-sum instance.

use_restrictions: Literature statement with precise source-linked proof maps; no whole-paper reproof or formal verification.

Pay final statistical accuracy once after coarse proximal progress.

summary: Dimension-uniform fixed raw-call minimax complexity is tilde Θ(A+B+C+D_G), with explicit G-independent polylogarithmic prefactor and additive dual-residual localization logarithm.
title: Sharp localized fresh-gradient NC–SC minimax complexity with four additive terms
use_when: Compare deterministic progress, global stochastic progress, final statistical accuracy and initial dual localization costs under the specified fresh-gradient oracle.
